notes:
No files edited. Includes all 48 Table 1 rows and six additional observations; Oman is covered by K12. Every observation has exactly one main interpretation. Repository quotations were selected as exact substrings; short table quotations support the printed age, while locators and notes carry the assemblage context. Source IDs retain wellman2022 for the 2022 online publication despite the 2023 volume date. All DOI fields are deliberately blank: publisher/repository DOI strings were encountered, but Crossref verification was unavailable. Unknown access means access to the full source was not established; it is allowed by the supplied JSON schema, although the README lists only open/closed/print.

Age encoding: a trailing question mark on a single stage is represented by that stage and its next younger neighbour: Hirnantian–Rhuddanian, Katian–Hirnantian, Dapingian–Darriwilian. This is an explicit operational reading of the requested uncertain-side rule, not a newly established geological correlation. Katian-Hirnantian? remains Katian–Hirnantian as instructed. Footnote markers are not age question marks. Cambrian stage fields remain blank because the authoritative timescale contains no Cambrian stages; extend it before using those records numerically.

Q1 pivotal records: accepting either Swedish Sandbian trilete horizon moves secure E1 from Katian to Sandbian. These horizons must remain separate; 459.1 Ma belongs to Hooper's soft maximum based on the 48.2 m probable Chelinospora, not the younger 41.9 m Ambitisporites specimen. Accepting the Argentine Dapingian cryptospores moves E2 one stage older than definitive Darriwilian occurrences. However Dp1 independently permits Dapingian Saudi cryptospores, so rejecting Argentina alone does not eliminate all Dapingian possibilities. Cambrian or Tremadocian embryophyte affinity would move E2 much farther back. Hooper's reassignment of regular cryptospore producers to stem embryophytes does not itself exclude them from E2, which is an embryophyte event rather than a crown-membership event.

Q5: footnote * explicitly rejects pre-Sandbian Swedish cryptospores; it does not reject all of S2 or prove either Sandbian trilete mark an artefact. The extra Furudal observation preserves that distinction. The existing W13-008-trilete entry deserves review: its appendix taxon is Ambitisporites vavrdovii, and the project vetting already cautions that broken tetrad monads do not establish true triletes. Existing W13-013, W13-014 and W13-023 trilete labels also warrant source-level reconciliation before deriving an E1 first appearance from pooled assemblages. Their labels were not treated here as automatic proof of triletes in each narrower Table 1 stage.

Deduplication limitation: several table rows are regional aggregates containing multiple publications or samples. Links to existing pooled assemblages denote that overlap and must not erase separately resolved stage occurrences or specimen horizons. In particular K3/S1, K13/S5 and Qusaiba regional/sample records require interval-aware deduplication; the schema's single same_material_as field cannot fully represent these many-to-many relationships. Blank links mean an exact assemblage match was not established, not that no overlap exists. The Saudi depth discrepancy is real in the existing extraction: Table 2 and Hooper print 551.0 m, whereas captions use ft; retain it unresolved.

Full papers still needed for stronger primary checking include Spina (2015), Steemans et al. (1996), Rubinstein et al. (2010), Wellman et al. (2003) and the complete Strother and Foster (2021) text. No closed-literature register changes were made because editing was prohibited. No modelling or numerical first-appearance analysis was run. Memory was consulted only for project orientation; all occurrence claims above were checked against sources read during this task.
